technical.summary: Short-term momentum signals (Hull, MACD) show early bullish structure, but price remains below all major moving averages and cloud with weak volume, creating conflicting intermediate-term bearish context unsuitable for high-probability swing entry.

fundamental.summary: TT shows no fundamental conviction signals with zero insider activity, no institutional positioning, absent government contracts, no lobbying presence, and minimal retail interest; earnings in 71 days adds timing risk.

sentiment.congressional_conviction: medium — moderate amounts, junior-to-mid tier members
sentiment.summary: Extreme fear (10/10) with recent congressional buys presents contrarian opportunity, though conviction is moderate and news data unavailable for confirmation.

risk.summary: Extreme VIX crisis regime (384.48) with flat yield curve creates severe macro headwinds; earnings in 71 days poses minimal near-term binary risk but overall environment is highly unfavourable for trading.

debate.key_bull_argument: Hull flip, MACD crossover, and supertrend bullish with extreme fear sentiment and congressional buys create early momentum structure at support (123.05) with contrarian opportunity.
debate.key_bear_argument: Price trapped below all major moving averages and Ichimoku cloud with weak volume (0.68 ratio), zero fundamental conviction, VIX crisis regime (384.48), and RSI bearish divergence make this a low-probability entry in severely unfavourable macro conditions.

decision.entry_rationale: Early momentum signals (Hull flip, MACD crossover) present at support level with extreme fear sentiment offering contrarian setup. However, price remains structurally trapped below all major moving averages and Ichimoku cloud with weak volume confirmation, creating low-probability entry conditions.
decision.primary_risk: VIX crisis regime (384.48) and macro headwinds combined with price below all key technical levels mean any entry is fighting severe structural and environmental resistance; stop loss will be frequently tested.
